defect_title: Count API cardinality estimation error with exact:false exceeds 10% tolerance and exhibits non-linear, direction-flipping behavior across collection sizes
finding_summary: The count API's exact:false mode uses index-based cardinality estimation that produces significant errors (5-13%) on range filters. Error magnitude exceeds tolerated estimation thresholds and exhibits non-linear, direction-flipping behavior across collection sizes, proving this is NOT a by-design fallback heuristic.
expected_behavior: count(exact:false) should return results within 10% of count(exact:true) and scroll ground truth, or should indicate when estimation confidence is low.
actual_behavior: Errors range from -13.3% to +5% depending on collection size and filter bounds. Error direction is inconsistent (under vs over estimate) and does not scale linearly with size, distinguishing it from by-design heuristics.
reproduction_steps: 2. Insert N points with indexed field (price) in range distribution
3. Create payload index on price field
5. Call POST /collections/{c}/points/count with filter: range(300-500), exact:true
6. Call POST /collections/{c}/points/count with filter: range(300-500), exact:false
8. Verify error > 10% OR direction flips across collection sizes

test_linear_scaling.description: Test if error scales linearly with collection size (would indicate by-design fallback)
test_linear_scaling.result: FAILED - error does NOT scale linearly

test_consistent_direction.description: Test if error direction is consistent across sizes
test_consistent_direction.evidence: Inconsistent error direction indicates genuine estimator bug, not design heuristic

test_magnitude_tolerance.description: Test if error magnitude exceeds 10% tolerance

ground_truth_validation.conclusion: exact:false is inaccurate, exact:true is ground truth

control_group_verification.overall_verdict: NOT by-design - genuine estimator bug in index histogram calculation

threat_model_reference.rationale: Team assumes payload indexes work correctly for all filter types without testing edge cases like range estimation accuracy

by_design_exclusions.conclusion: All by-design tests FAILED, confirming genuine defect

wontfix_considerations: Estimation accuracy may be improved with larger histogram samples
May require architectural changes to index estimator
Team may deprioritize as enhancement rather than defect

submission_strategy.rationale: Historical precedent: Issue #10096 (cardinality under-count with is_null) was acknowledged. This is a different condition class (range filter) but same estimator surface. Control group evidence strong.
submission_strategy.recommended_title: count(exact:false) range filter estimation error exceeds 10% with non-linear behavior
submission_strategy.evidence_to_attach: Control group test results showing non-linear, direction-flipping error across collection sizes

novelty_assessment.rationale: Same estimator bug surface as #10096, but different filter condition (range vs is_null) producing distinct error pattern (non-linear vs linear)

impact_analysis.affected_queries: All count API calls with exact:false and range filters on indexed integer fields
impact_analysis.affected_users: Applications using count for analytics, pagination, or resource planning
impact_analysis.consequence: Under- or over-estimated cardinality may cause inefficient query plans or incorrect UI pagination
impact_analysis.mitigation: Use exact:true for critical queries, be aware of estimation errors

next_tests: Test other filter condition classes (geo_radius, match_any, is_empty) on exact:false
Test compound filters with must/must_not combinations
Test with different index configurations (different ranges, different field types)
Cross-pollinate to other endpoints with estimation behavior (recommend, search aggregations)
